ratings_why.fun: Loading a line to two pips and lighting one end is a satisfying fuse to build, and spend-or-hold gives every board a real choice.
ratings_why.distinct: News spilling along the zigzag is a cascade no current tribe has, though touching runs echo Hedgerow and it lands near chain-lightning combo tribes.

verdict_why: Two small rules holes remain (copied caps on the Thirty-Two, Fips's tie); the rest reads well and should settle after that.

points.text: The Thirty-Two copies only the printed Blurt text, but the Landlady's 3-gold cap sits outside her Blurt text, so the copy gains gold with no cap. Say copied texts keep their limits, or move the cap into the Blurt text.
Little Fips's 'unit farthest from this along the zigzag' has no tie rule when Fips sits mid-line. Add one, such as the later one in reading order.
Ilse's text is wordy for a Tier 3 card. 'Start of Turn: Gossip 1 to each of your units that had 2 Gossip.' carries the same timing in one line.
Standing pips and fight pips look the same but behave differently. Show fight Gossip in its own colour so a player can see the board reload after the fight.
The Cold-Shed Tangle's 'twice a turn and twice a fight' is two counters on one card. One limit, 'twice per chain', would read faster and still stop runaway Strays.

standouts.why: The Bad Omen turns the tribe's rule on the enemy: gossip spreading through their board and hurting them is both a fresh play and the knot's bad-omen lore.
Little Fips is the one rat who sees the far end, and his card throws news to the far end. Flavour and function match at a glance.
The Bean-Counter counts the vote: it pays for each rat that Blurted before it, so a player knows to put it last.

weakest.why: The Wall-Runner is a plain Discover with a chain count attached; the wall-runway fantasy doesn't show in what it does.
Ilse the Minute-Taker reads like a rules clause, not a card, though the job fits her story.
The Cold-Shed Tangle's double limit is hard to track at a glance.

flags.note: Whether limits on copied texts (Landlady's gold cap, Tangle's twice-a-turn) apply to the Thirty-Two is not stated.
A fully loaded board under the Piper attacks seven times at Start of Combat, which may decide fights before the other side acts.
Golden Thirty-Two with a golden Bellringer under the King uses each text many times a turn; worth the owner's eye.
